newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ugandan president to Paris to discuss Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan president to Paris to discuss Zaire.

text.p: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, a key player in the Zaire crisis, is expected in Paris next week for talks about the explosive situation in the Great Lakes area of central Africa, French officials said on Thursday.
No specific date was mentioned for the visit by Museveni whose country is accused by Zaire of sending troops into Zaire to back Tutsi rebels advancing on four fronts against government forces.
French officials will also receive Burundi Foreign Minister Luc Rukingama whose country also is involved in the crisis.
France, which has traditionally backed Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko, said on Thursday it was "especially attentive" to the presence of foreign troops in Zaire.
The United States on Wednesday said it had urged Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi to stay out of the fighting in east Zaire.
Zaire has accused all three of sending their troops into eastern Zaire to fight alongside the rebels. All three countries, which border on rebel-held territory, deny doing so.
Paris said it agreed with Washington that the participation of foreign forces in the Zaire conflict would "create a situation of great gravity."

A foreign ministry statement reiterated France's stance that a U.N. and Organisation of African Unity (OAU) backed international conference should be held on the crisis and Zaire should be helped to organise a referendum and elections.
